Mr. Naman Bagrecha – IIFL Capital Services Limited: 
 
- 
Thank you Tanvi. Good afternoon everyone. On behalf of IIFL Capital Services Limited, 
we welcome you all to Granules India 2.0 Comprehensive Transformation Underway 
webinar with Granules promoters and senior management team to understand the key 
growth engines. We will begin the call with the opening commentary from Dr. Krishna 
Prasad Chigurupati, Chairman and Managing Director, followed by Ms. Priyanka 
Chigurupati, ED, Mr. Vijay, President Granules Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Mr. Sanjay Kumar, 
CEO Senn Tides India Private Limited, and Mr. Mukesh Surana, CFO Granules, which will 
be followed by a Q&A session. Over to you, doctor. 
 
- 
Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati  - Chairman & Managing Director, Granules India 
Limited: 
 
- 
Thank you, Naman, and a very good afternoon everyone, and thank you very much for 
joining us today. Over the last few years, many conversations around Granules have 
understandably focused on regulatory journey, our earnings quality, earnings recovery, 
and the challenges we face as an organization. Today, I would like to shift that 
conversation. I would like to spend a few minutes talking about what comes next for 
Granules.  
 
- 
After nearly three years of relatively flat performance, we returned to growth in FY26. 
For me, this was a very important milestone, but I view it not as a destination, but the 
beginning of a new journey and a growth cycle for the company. Over the last several 
years, we have invested significantly in manufacturing infrastructure, in R&D, in product 
development, and building new capabilities. Today, we are moving from building these 
capabilities to scaling them and converting them into commercial growth. The slide you 
see in front of you captures how we think about this journey.   
 
- 
At the foundation is our established business built on manufacturing excellence, vertical 
integration, scale, and cost competitiveness. This business remains central to Granules. 
It generates cash, supports our balance sheet, and provides a platform from which we 

 2
can invest in future growth. Building on that foundation, we have identified four growth 
engines, control substances, complex generics and early market opportunities, 
oncologies, and peptide CDMO. These are not four independent bets. They are built on 
capabilities we already possess while giving us multiple venues for growth across 
different products, markets, and timelines. 
 
- 
Beyond these growth engines, we continue to evaluate additional opportunities and 
expand our geographic reach. Because even as today's businesses scale up, we must 
continue building the next generation of growth. Our objective over the next three to 
four years is straightforward. To translate these investments into a substantially larger 
business with earnings growing faster as our portfolio becomes more differentiated and 
operating leverage develops. And equally importantly, we intend to do so while 
maintaining the financial discipline that has always been fundamental to Granules.  
 
- 
With that context, let me hand over to Priyanka who will take you through our product 
strategy, R&D priorities, and opportunities that exist. Over to you, Priyanka.  
 
- 
Ms. Priyanka Chigurupati – Executive Director, Granules India Limited: 
 
- 
Thank you, CMD. You've outlined the four engines of our next growth cycle. I'd like to 
focus a little bit on portfolio, R&D strategy, and market strategy that underpins this 
transformation. Our next phase is not simply about efficient manufacturing at scale and 
selling more products. It's about generating greater value from each successful 
development program. Our vertically integrated manufacturing platform remains the 
foundation. What is changing is, how we deploy that foundation and our R&D 
capabilities to capture new growth opportunities.  
 
- 
Our evolving growth strategy. The next phase of growth is fundamentally different from 
the last. While scale, manufacturing, efficiency, and cost competitiveness have been 
central to our success, while we continue to nurture them, the future growth is 
increasingly going to be driven by higher value products, with products being extended 
to other markets, an improved portfolio mix, and greater operating leverage. Over the 
past several years, we've invested significantly in R&D, manufacturing, infrastructure, 
and advanced formulation capabilities. A substantial part of this foundation is already in 
place.  
 
- 
Our priority now is to convert these investments into commercial opportunities and 
generate greater value from our existing assets. Our vertically integrated platform 
spanning APIs through to finish dosages remains a fundamental competitive advantage. 
We intend to leverage this foundation not to simply increase volumes, but to develop 
and manufacture more differentiated products using existing knowledge and improve 
the quality of our earnings. On our portfolio transformation, perhaps the most 
significant change taking place within our R&D and product development strategy is our 

 3
first-to-file playbook. Historically, growth in generics has often been associated with the 
number of products developed and filed. Our approach is increasingly selective.  
 
- 
Product selection is guided by technical complexity, patient needs that are unmet, 
competitive intensity, intellectual property considerations, and economics of market 
entry. This strategy has been demonstrated through the contribution of complex 
generics that increased from 1% of overall revenue in fiscal 20 to 33% of overall revenue 
in fiscal 26. And as a part of, as a percentage of overall finished dosages, the 
contribution of complex is roughly 45 to 50% in fiscal 26. We are prioritizing 
opportunities where our formulation expertise, vertical integration, and manufacturing 
capabilities can create meaningful differentiation. We're building a broader pipeline of 
differentiated opportunities across controlled substances, oncology, and other complex 
generics with further filings planned over the coming years. Our first-to-file strategy is 
the clearest evidence of that transformation. We've already filed two sole first-to-file 
ANDAs, marking an important milestone in the evolution of our R&D capabilities. 
Generic Lumryz and Generic Dyanavel have a combined market size north of 350 million 
US dollars, just in the US, where we would potentially have 180-day exclusivity. 
 
- 
We have filed another product, which we believe would be a sole FDF in the oncology 
category. Over the next few years, we have a pipeline of four to five other first-to-files, 
all of which would commercialize between fiscal 30 and 34. This reflects a clear and 
visible change in Granules' R&D story. These opportunities have a different commercial 
profile from conventional generics. Successful early market entry with 180-day or more 
of exclusivity, particularly in products with significant technical and regulatory barriers, 
can create substantial commercial value. The timing and realization of these 
opportunities depend on regulatory approvals, intellectual property outcomes, and 
market conditions, and consequently, individual successful launches hold potential to 
generate lumpy upsides. 
 
- 
Importantly, we are building a repeatable development strategy with an objective to 
improve the potential commercial value of each successful development program. 
Geographical expansion further strengthens this approach. By extending select products 
across international markets, customers, and distribution channels, we intend to 
generate additional value from our R&D investments and established manufacturing 
capabilities and setups. 
 
- 
On our oncology business, our oncology business represents another important 
application of this evolving strategy. We have reassessed our approach, shifting from a 
broad portfolio of conventional oncology generics towards selected molecules, where 
technical complexity, differentiated formulations, and early market entry offer stronger 
commercial potential. This strategy builds on our existing API and finished dosage 
development capabilities, complemented by advanced formulation technologies, 
including amorphous solid dispersions. Our priorities include carefully selected first-to-
file, paragraph four, and other early entry opportunities. We will leverage our existing 

 4
oncology manufacturing infrastructure in Vizag, facing additional investments against 
development programs, regulatory milestones, and commercial opportunities. We 
expect oncology to become an additional growth contributor as the pipeline progresses 
towards commercialization over the coming years. 
 
- 
Our controlled products pipeline extends through Fiscal 35, while our oncology 
portfolio, which begins commercialization in Fiscal 29, extends through Fiscal 35. 
Ultimately, our portfolio transformation emphasizes selective investment, technical 
differentiation, strategic market entry, and broader commercialization, generating 
greater value from our scientific capabilities, manufacturing assets, and R&D 
investments.  
 
- 
On the market front, the U.S., which currently represents approximately 75 percent of 
the overall revenue, will remain our anchor market. But the way we compete in the U.S. 
is evolving. Today, Granules' U.S. presence is primarily concentrated on the retail side 
across OTC and prescription products. Our expanding portfolio will allow us to enter the 
specialty and institutional segments, with our first product expected to launch in Fiscal 
29. We're also launching our B2C division in Canada next year, which will enable us to 
maximize the value per asset filed in the region.  
 
- 
At the same time, we're deliberately building the second geographic leg of Granules, 
which is primarily API and PFI-led in Europe and ROW markets. Fiscal 30, we intend to 
establish a meaningful presence across Latin America and other strategic international 
markets using a combination of B2B and B2C channels. When it comes to R&D, the U.S. 
will always remain the anchor country where, going forward, we aim to file between 10 
and 15 products per year, which will further be extended to Europe and rest of the 
world countries. Objective is not geographic expansion for its own sake. It is to take 
products and capabilities that Granules already understands exceptionally well and 
monetize them across a much larger global footprint. 
 
- 
To bring everything together, our portfolio strategy is evolving in three important ways. 
We're becoming more selective in product development, increasingly pursuing 
differentiated and early market opportunities, and extending the potential value of our 
R&D investments across products and geographies. Oncology represents an important 
application of this strategy for the future. Controlled substances demonstrate what 
these capabilities can already achieve at scale.  
 
- 
Vijay will now take you through how we have built that franchise, the competitive 
advantages supporting it, and the growth runway ahead. On to you, Vijay.

Mr. Vijay Ramanavarapu – President, Granules Pharmaceuticals, Inc.:  
 
- 
Thank you, Priyanka. Good afternoon. I'd like to focus on one of the clearest growth 
engines in our U.S. business, controlled substances. As per the latest IQVIA data, 

 5
Granules is now the third largest controlled substance manufacturer in the United 
States by value. In July 2025, we were eighth. This segment helps make Granules 
Pharma our front-end RX division amongst the 10 fastest growing generics companies 
by absolute dollars in 2025 for the second year in a row. This is a market with high 
barriers to entry. In addition to needing FDA approval, controlled substances are also 
regulated by the DEA, which grants quota to each manufacturer.  
 
- 
We primarily focus on Schedule II products, which require the API and the finished 
dosage to be made in the U.S. We've been building this capability since we actively 
launched in 2018, and it's hard to replicate quickly. Our core franchise is the ADHD 
space. This space primarily covers four molecules, Methylphenidate, 
Dexmethylphenidate, Amphetamines, and Lisdexamfetamine. We compete in all four 
molecules with eight products approved and seven actively marketed. 
 
- 
Our DEA quota has gone up every year, which shows the regulator's confidence in our 
reputable customer base, as well as our compliance record, including a DEA audit just 
last month. Our Chantilly facility also has room to grow, so we can continue growing 
share with our existing infrastructure. We've been successful due to a variety of 
reasons. 
 
- 
The quota system changed a few years ago, which caused shortages in the space and 
changed how wholesalers buy. The wholesalers moved their business to suppliers they 
can rely on, and we're one of them. We deliver our control substances with a near 100% 
service level. We've also qualified or developed several API vendors, so we usually 
receive our full API allocation when we get quota. We also have an N-1 model, where 
we make the intermediate in India and finish in the US. This gives us resilience that most 
competitors don't have. This supply diversification resonates with our major wholesalers 
who value supply security. The results show it. We are in the top three in six of the 
seven ADHD products that we market. In Adderall XR, our share went from 5% in 2024 
to 29% as of last month. In Lisdexamfetamine, we are now the number two generic 
supplier, even though we are the last person to enter the market space. The bigger 
opportunity is what lays ahead. 
 
- 
In Methylphenidate, we only address 6% of the market value today, and our pipeline 
covers 87% of the value, with launches starting in the next several months. In 
Dexmethylphenidate, we've been approved for 39% of the value, with another 50% in 
the pipeline. In Amphetamines, our approvals cover 74% of the value, but we haven't 
yet promoted Adderall IR, which is one of the largest products. We'll launch it in the 
coming months, along with another amphetamine product.  
 
- 
We're also opening a second gross ligand pain management. We've entered opioids in 
the past year. Granules is one of only two vertically integrated suppliers of paracetamol, 
which gives us a structural cost and supply advantage. We have two ANDAs in the 
market, and more filings planned.

- 
Finally, we're pursuing first-to-file opportunities. First-to-files are more attractive in the 
controlled substances space than elsewhere in generics. Competition is naturally 
limited, so the usual price drop on day 181 is often much smaller. In some cases, there's 
only one competitor or none. 
 
- 
To sum it up, we've built a scale to comply in a reliable position in the market, with real 
barriers to entry. We have a defensible moat, and we have a visible pipeline of launches 
in the short, mid, and long term. We believe this business still has a long runway for 
growth.

Mr. Sanjay Kumar – CEO, Senn Tides India Private Limited:

Well, thank you, Vijay. We have just heard how Granules built its controlled substances 
businesses through sustained investment in R&D, manufacturing, and commercial 
execution. Our ambition is to replicate that success in peptide CDMO, but on a 
compressed timeline. We entered this business last year through the acquisition of Senn 
Chemicals in Switzerland. That brought us six decades of peptide chemistry excellence 
and a long-standing relationship with innovators. 
 
- 
Our strategy is quite straightforward. We intend to combine Swiss expertise and 
customer access that comes with it, with the Indian manufacturing scale, scientific 
talent, and in the end, cost competitiveness. For many innovative customers, 
Switzerland remains the preferred starting point for development, initial supplies, and 
relationship management. India provides the opportunity to scale those programs 
competitively.  
 
- 
Our second differentiation is technology. CEN has particular expertise in liquid phase 
peptide synthesis, and that has become mainstream as the peptide has become larger 
and larger in size and moving from a kilogram scale to a ton scale. And also to support 
customers from the early development to the commercial supplies, we are also 
complementing this LPPS technology with a solid phase and hybrid synthesis capability, 
both in Switzerland and in India. I also want to stress onto the fact that today we are 
simultaneously transforming and expanding the business as we have taken over this 
business about 18 months ago. In Switzerland, we are strengthening execution, 
upgrading infrastructure, expanding capabilities, and deepening customer relationships. 
 
- 
In India, our Hyderabad R&D center is already operational, and we are advancing 
manufacturing expansion as we speak starting this month with land allocated to our 
peptide CDMO entity, which will support both peptide intermediates and peptide APIs. 
Commercially, our focus is on converting growing customer engagement into a 
sustained development and manufacturing relationship.

- 
It's important that I turn attention to our financial ambition as well. While our 
immediate financial priority is to become profitable this year, that is FY27, we have set 
out one intermediate and one long-term goal for ourselves. We are targeting 
approximately 50 million US dollar in annual revenue run rate in three years from now 
as an intermediate milestone to get to and cross the threshold of 100 million revenue 
size in five years.  
 
- 
Finally, our ambition actually extends beyond peptides and cover some near-side 
opportunity on oligonucleotide and subsequently to ADC-related capabilities. We have 
already initiated our entry into oligonucleotides and are evaluating ADC-related 
capabilities, approaching both through a discipline and a phased investment approach. 
Our objective is to establish Senn Tides India Private Limited as a meaningful mid-size 
global CDMO platform. We believe that our established Senn Foundation combined with 
the Indian scale and the granular execution capability as demonstration and control 
substance franchise, which Vijay and Priyanka spoke to you about, provides a credible 
pathway to that ambition. 
 
- 
With that, I'll hand it over to Mukesh, who will explain how our financial strength and 
capital allocation priorities support these growth ambitions.

Mr. Mukesh Surana – CFO, Granules India Limited:

Good evening, everyone. You've heard the growth strategy from our leaders. Let me 
connect it to our financial performance, capital allocation and investment plans. Our 
transformation is already strengthening financial performance. Over four years, gross 
margin expanded by about 15 percentage points to 65 percent and EBITDA margin by 
three percentage points to 22 percent. 
 
- 
At the same time, R&D investment rose from about 3 percent of revenue a few years 
ago to 6 percent in Q1 FY27, improving the quality of sales growth. This reflects our shift 
to differentiated products, especially complex generics, backed by stronger formulation 
and development capabilities. Growth has also been supported by strong cash 
generation and better capital efficiency. Cash flow from operations averaged about 73 
percent of our EBITDA over the last four years. We generated positive cash, free cash 
flow consistently, funded our growth and reduced our debt leverage. While ROCE 
improved by about one percentage point year on year to 18 percent. 
 
- 
With the balance sheet strengthening with the balance proceeds which we have 
received from the preferential warrants in September 2026, we are now in a 
consolidated net cash position. This positions us to invest in our next phase of growth. 
Our capital allocation priorities are aligned with these balance sheet strength.

We plan to invest about 2,000 crore in organic capital expenditure over the next three 
to four years, supporting complex generics pipeline, oncology pipeline, peptide CDMO, 
US operations, manufacturing and R&D infrastructure. We will also invest in 
digitalization, AI manufacturing excellence and quality system to enhance productivity, 
resilience and competitiveness. Importantly, these investments will follow a disciplined 
milestone based approach, aligning capital deployment with development progress, 
regulatory milestones, customer commitments and commercial opportunities. 
 
- 
As our genome value and peptide CDMO investments progress through their respective 
ramp up phases, we see opportunities for further improvement in profitability and ROCE 
over the medium term. Our objective is not to simply increase our investment base, it is 
to progressively improve the quality and sustainability of earnings while generating 
healthy returns on the capital we deploy.  
 
- 
In summary, our strengthened financial position allows us to fund our strategic 
ambitions while maintaining financial discipline. We believe this combination of 
differentiated growth opportunities, disciplined investment and improving capital 
productivity provides a strong foundation for sustainable growth and long term 
shareholder value. Thank you.
